Life from age 4 to 16

I like asking what happens behind the scenes. People remember that I help with football and assume I want everything to involve sports, but I also spend a lot of time writing ridiculous conversations.

  • family: Lives with his father and aunt; cousins visit most weekends.
  • finances: Father’s utility job covers essentials; larger purchases require saving.
  • geography: Small town outside San Angelo, Texas.
  • cultureLanguages: English and conversational Spanish; extended family gatherings feature regional music.
  • school: Small public high school with a shared agricultural shop.
  • accessOpportunities: School bus and library internet; limited local clubs outside athletics.
  • Age 4–5

    In 2014, Elias followed his aunt through grocery shopping and asked why identical cans cost different amounts. At home he sorted bottle caps into elaborate arrangements that he changed whenever someone guessed the rule.

  • Age 6–7

    In 2016, he joined a children’s dance group with cousins. He remembered sequences easily but disliked the stiff performance clothes. His father built a backyard shade frame, and Elias wanted to help measure everything.

  • Age 8–9

    At eight in 2018, he began making detailed maps for imaginary bus routes. A teacher let him explain one to the class; he enjoyed questions about the route more than displaying the drawing itself.

  • Age 10–11

    In 2020, unreliable home internet made remote lessons frustrating. His aunt printed assignments at work, and Elias completed them at the kitchen table while helping a cousin invent indoor obstacle courses between video calls.

  • Age 12–13

    At twelve, he tried school football because practice provided a late bus. By 2023 he preferred maintaining equipment and keeping statistics, though he still liked the feeling of being part of the sideline group.

  • Age 14–15

    During 2024, Elias began earning weekend money stocking a feed store. He learned product locations and asked customers how they used unfamiliar supplies. In 2025 he also started writing short comic scenes with a friend.

  • Age 16

    In 2026, he is saving for a used laptop and exploring an open house at a Texas technical college. He also wants to see a college theater rehearsal, something he has never watched beyond school productions. He recently asked the librarian to help compare workshop dates before mentioning the idea at home.

Life now

  • enjoys: Route maps · Comic dialogue · Group dancing
  • avoids: Being rushed through explanations · Full-contact games
  • activities: Feed-store shifts · Equipment help · Writing with a friend
  • demonstratedSkills: Accurate stock counts · Spatial sketches · Remembering dance sequences
  • unfamiliarActivities: College residence halls · Advanced coding · Theater lighting
  • motivations: Being dependable · Seeing how systems fit together
  • ambitions: Spend a summer in a larger city · Find a program with both practical and creative options · He imagines living independently within visiting distance of family, with a useful workshop and friends who make him laugh.
  • struggles: Keeps postponing unfamiliar applications · Quiet when adults assume his interests
  • supports: Father · Aunt · Store supervisor
  • practicalConstraints: Weekend work · Long travel to campuses · Limited home broadband

Still uncertain: Would a larger setting feel freeing or exhausting? · Does he prefer stock work itself or the knowledgeable conversations around it?
